Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{RQ}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{PT}=b,$ and  $\overset{\to }{RT}=c.$ Find $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ in terms of the vectors $a,b,$ and $c.$ To denote the corresponding vectors, use $a$, $b,$ and $c.$

$\overset{\to }{PQ}=$   
 {{field-1}}
worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $P$ to $Q$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{PQ}=\overset{\to }{PT}+\overset{\to }{TR}+\overset{\to }{RQ}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/6bfe5ad7a1695d5208504f1666014737b020976d73419f4be273b5a84097e242.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{PT}=b,\,\overset{\to }{TR}=-c,\,\overset{\to }{RQ}=a.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/86a8fb7563c4a8874fc6d9b460c8e93bcf2c96e1b4e63a4f56f49f7326d2dcca.png)

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =\overset{\to }{PT}+\overset{\to }{TR}+\overset{\to }{RQ} \\  & =b-c+a.\end{aligned}
$$
